entries.claim_boundary: Certifies an exact finite-resolution approximate-identity theorem for the conditional charged-time event-map chain contract, including BV descent, charged covariance, support inheritance, distributional convergence, profile error/composition bounds and conditional frequency-ratio error control. It does not certify a nonzero counterflow receiver, detector, redshift, global monotone compact clock, nonlinear dynamics, phenomenology or quantum observable.

dispersion.statement: Exact profile scaling, moment addition and charged action-angle covariance are certified; no wave dispersion is inferred.

lee_wald.statement: The imported Darboux pair is nondegenerate; receiver nontriviality and any theory-specific descended pairing remain conditional.

resonance.statement: Finite-resolution sampling does not decide a background-specific resonance.

bounded_or_finite_quasiperiodic.statement: Requires a theory-specific receiver and correction class.

causal_retarded.statement: Support inheritance is certified conditionally, but no theory-specific Green image or receiver class is supplied.

smooth_secular.statement: Sampling and phase-map composition bounds do not supply a nonlinear secular correction.

taub_maps.statement: No theory-specific second-order source or nonlinear receiver is part of this theorem.

scope.background: any oriented spacetime satisfying the imported event-map and declared compact-support hypotheses
scope.boundaries: compact receiver support; epsilon profile band in a regular lifted clock chart, or declared periodicized S1 profile
scope.carrier: conditional compact receiver bicomplex class [A], action-angle pair (psi,Q), and normalized even compact profile kappa
scope.charge_sector: unrestricted physical Q; charged R and D with K=D-H'(Q)R
scope.ell: all receiver modes satisfying the contract
scope.omega: finite sampled band with H'(Q) fixed nonzero sign on the lifted chart
scope.parity: profile even; receiver cooriented under primitive clock reversal
scope.theory: Hamiltonian/BV theories with one surviving physical action-angle clock pair
